subject: Request: split advance + quarterly invoicing for ArborMed pilot
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <procurement@arbormed.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Kline <cfo@arbormed.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Payment terms request for pilot (SOW attached)

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. We'd like to move forward with the 6-month pilot as scoped in the attached SOW, but our procurement team needs an adjusted invoicing cadence to align with fiscal planning. Proposed approach:

- 30% advance invoiced and payable within 7 days of SOW signing
- Remaining 70% invoiced quarterly in arrears on Net-90 terms (i.e., each quarterly invoice due 90 days after issuance)

We understand this is outside standard terms — the advance covers setup and initial onboarding costs; Net-90 for the remainder is critical for our cashflow coordination. We are prepared to provide a PO immediately and run this as a pilot with one production tenant.

Attached: SOW_ArborMed_v3.pdf

Let me know what you need from our side to get approvals.

Best,
Alice Morgan
Director, Procurement
ArborMed Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Payment terms request for pilot (SOW attached)

Forwarding ArborMed's request — procurement wants 30% advance + quarterly invoices on Net-90 for the remainder. Deal details: 6-month pilot, estimated TCV $420,000 (annualized ~$840k if expanded). Customer is strategic in healthcare vertical; pilot expected to accelerate to dedicated next year.

Why this matters: sales wants to keep momentum; they will sign PO immediately if we accept terms. Financial impact: pushing Net-90 on 70% increases DSO materially for Q4. We have a proposed one-time concession of 5-10% on first-year ARR to sweeten the deal (sales asked for 10%).

Please advise approval path. Marcus — do you need a credit check? Vanessa — can you justify the concession vs. risk? I'm happy to join a quick call.

Attachments: SOW_ArborMed_v3.pdf

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Deal Desk / Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Payment terms request for pilot (SOW attached)

Mina — thanks for flagging. A few points from finance: 

1) Credit & risk: We need a recent credit reference and bank reference before we accept extended terms beyond Net-30. I pulled an internal preliminary credit summary (see attached ArborMed_credit_report.xlsx) — large health system, but there are a couple of historical late-payment notes.

2) Alternative suggestion: Approve the 30% advance as requested, but reduce the remainder terms to Net-60 for the pilot instead of Net-90. Net-60 materially lowers our DSO exposure and is a reasonable middle ground.

3) If we must do Net-90, require one of the following mitigations: a) escrow for the first quarterly invoice, or b) bank guarantee, or c) apply a 5% non-refundable onboarding fee charged upfront (separate from the 30% advance).

4) Concession: finance is uncomfortable with a 10% first-year concession. Recommend capping at 5% and applying it as a one-time credit on first invoice only.

I can run the credit request with AR and legal can prepare simple language for the payment hold / escrow.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Finance, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Payment terms request for pilot (SOW attached)

Mina / Marcus — quick context from Sales: ArborMed is in a multi-hospital roll-out pilot and is pushing multiple vendors into a single PO for simplicity. If we ask them to move to Net-60 they may delay or split vendors — risk of losing the seat. The pilot is strategically valuable for our healthcare GTM and could convert to a $1.6M dedicated arrangement within 12 months.

Proposed compromise that protects us while keeping the deal:
- Accept 30% advance and invoice it immediately on SOW signing (payment due in 7 days).
- Invoice remaining 70% quarterly in arrears, but set payment term to Net-90 with the following conditions: 
  a) 5% one-time concession (applied as credit on the first invoice), not 10%
  b) Signed PO + DocuSign SOW before any work begins
  c) Finance to run credit check and confirm no older than 90-day late-payment flags within 48 hours
  d) If credit check flags issues, switch to escrow or Net-60 at Redwood's discretion

I think this preserves momentum and reduces our downside. If legal and finance can put the right language in the SOW (payment hold / remedy), we should be able to accept.

I recommend exec sign-off on the conditional Net-90 given strategic upside. Happy to jump on a 20-min call.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Approved (conditions) — ArborMed pilot payment terms

Team — after reviewing the ask and the anticipated strategic value, I approve proceeding with the conditional Net-90 on the 70% remainder for the pilot with the following binding conditions: 

1) 30% advance invoiced and paid within 7 days of DocuSign SOW execution. Work does not commence until payment is received.
2) 5% one-time concession only, applied as a credit on the first invoice (no ongoing discounting).
3) Customer must sign DocuSign SOW + provide PO before the advance is invoiced.
4) Finance (Marcus) to run expedited credit checks and confirm no outstanding >90-day defaults within 48 hours. If credit checks flag issues, change remainder terms to Net-60 or require an escrow/bank guarantee.
5) Legal to include a payment remedy clause allowing Redwood to suspend service if a quarterly invoice is >60 days overdue during the pilot.
6) Deal Desk to log the special approval in HubSpot under deal ARB-2026-0421 and attach the signed SOW + credit evidence.

This is an exception for the pilot only. If the customer expands to a dedicated contract, payment terms revert to Redwood standard terms unless a new exec-level approval is recorded.

Approved by:
Aditya Rao
Chief Revenue Officer (on behalf of Deal Committee)
Redwood Inference
